questions.question: In triangle $ABD$, $AB = 3\,\text{cm}$ and $BD = 2\,\text{cm}$. Using Pythagoras’ theorem, find the length of $AD$.
questions.evidence: In $\triangle ABD$, by Pythagoras’ theorem, $AB^2 = AD^2 + BD^2$; $AD = \sqrt{3^2 - 2^2}\,\text{cm} = \sqrt{5}\,\text{cm}$
questions.subject: math

questions.question: In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AE = DC = 8\,\text{cm}$ and $AB = 18\,\text{cm}$. Find $EB$ and explain why $\angle AEC = \angle ADC$.
questions.referenceAnswer: $EB = AB - AE = 18 - 8 = 10\,\text{cm}$. Since $EC \parallel AD$, $AECD$ is a parallelogram, so opposite angles are equal: $\angle AEC = \angle ADC$.
questions.evidence: $EB = AB - AE = (18 - 8)\,\text{cm} = 10\,\text{cm}$; $\angle AEC = \angle ADC = 110^\circ \quad (\text{opp. } \angle s \text{ of //gram})$
questions.subject: math

questions.question: In triangle $BCE$, $\angle BEC = 70^\circ$, $\angle CBE = 38^\circ$, and $BC = 10\,\text{cm}$. Use the angle sum of a triangle to find $\angle BCE$, then use the sine formula to write an expression for $x = EC$.
questions.referenceAnswer: Since $\angle BCE + 70^\circ + 38^\circ = 180^\circ$, $\angle BCE = 72^\circ$. By the sine formula: $\frac{x}{\sin 70^\circ} = \frac{10}{\sin 72^\circ}$, so $x = \frac{10 \sin 70^\circ}{\sin 72^\circ}$ cm.

questions.question: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = 5\,\text{cm}$, $AC = 4\,\text{cm}$, and area $8\,\text{cm}^2$. Given that $\theta = \angle BAC$ is acute, find $\theta$ using the area formula.
questions.referenceAnswer: Using $\text{area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times AC \times \sin \theta$: $8 = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 \times \sin \theta$, so $\sin \theta = \frac{4}{5}$. Since $\theta$ is acute, $\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) \approx 53.1^\circ$.
questions.evidence: Area of $\triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times AC \times \sin A$; $8 = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 \times \sin \theta$; $\sin \theta = \frac{4}{5}$; $\theta = 53.130^\circ$ or $180^\circ - 53.130^\circ$ (reject); $= 53.1^\circ$

questions.question: In triangle $ABE$, $AE = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\,\text{cm}$, $BE = \frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}\,\text{cm}$, and $\sin \angle BAE = \frac{2}{3}$. Use the sine formula to find $\sin \theta$, where $\theta = \angle AEB$.
questions.referenceAnswer: By the sine formula: $\frac{AE}{\sin \theta} = \frac{BE}{\sin \angle BAE}$, so $\sin \theta = AE \cdot \frac{\sin \angle BAE}{BE} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2} \cdot \frac{2/3}{\sqrt{21}/2} = \frac{2\sqrt{105}}{63}$.
